Meta was built to help people connect and share, and over the last decade our tools have played a critical part in changing how people around the world communicate with one another. With over a billion people using the service and more than fifty offices around the globe, a career at Meta offers countless ways to make an impact in a fast growing organization.

Meta is seeking Research Interns to join our Post-Training & Research team within Facebook. The team is part of Facebook Discovery, which builds the systems that decide which posts, photos, videos and Reels people see on Facebook. Our team works on ranking and recommendation, content understanding, and post-training of the AI models behind agentic experiences on Facebook. Our interns will have the opportunity to turn open problems in these systems into research questions and work on them with our research scientists and engineers, with the potential for impact on billions of people.

We believe large language models (LLMs) and AI agents will change how recommendation systems are built. We study generative recommendation models that are trained like language models on sequences of user activity. We build ranking models that reason over a person’s history and a set of candidates to rank and compose what that person sees. We use multimodal models to understand the quality and originality of posts and videos. We post-train models with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning from user feedback, both for recommendation and for AI agents on Facebook. We deploy our models together with product and infrastructure teams, and we publish our results to advance the state of the art.

Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

Responsibilities

Define and lead a research project in machine learning for ranking and recommendation, with clear milestones over the course of the internship. Design, train and post-train deep learning models, from recommendation models to LLMs and AI agents, on Facebook-scale data. Evaluate models with offline metrics and online experiments, and analyze the results to decide the next iteration. Publish research results and contribute to research that can be applied to Meta product development. Collaborate with researchers and cross-functional partners including communicating research plans, progress, and results.

Join Method as part of our 2027 Summer Residency Program as a Product Management Resident and help build, ship, and learn as part of a small cross-functional team of Product, Design, and Engineering Residents.

Method is a strategic design and product development consultancy with 25 years of experience, and a GlobalLogic company within the Hitachi family. This residency is a hands-on way to see how a global digital consultancy works from the inside: you will discover user needs, define solutions, and drive development alongside the people who do this for clients every day.

Product management is changing quickly as AI takes on more of the research, synthesis, specification, and reporting work. We built this residency for people who want to learn the craft as it is being rewritten, not as it was practiced five years ago.

The role: Product Management for the AI era

The modern Product Manager is less a document producer and more a decision-maker who directs, checks and refines work done with AI. At Method we describe this as AI-native product management: you still own the "why" and the "what," but you use AI to move from research to a testable idea in days rather than weeks, and you apply judgment to what it produces.

As a Resident, you will practice the skills that set an AI-native PM apart:

- Framing the problem well. Writing clear specs and giving AI the right context, so the output is useful the first time.

- Working with AI as a teammate. Using AI for research synthesis, prototyping and drafting, and knowing which tasks to delegate and which to keep.

- Verifying, not trusting. Checking AI-generated work for accuracy, bias and fit with real user needs before it reaches a decision.

- Knowing where AI belongs. Judging where AI creates value for a user or business, and saying plainly where it will not pay off.

- Leading people through change. Helping teams adopt new tools and ways of working so they actually stick.

Because the work now spans more disciplines, the strongest PMs are increasingly hybrids. Method staffs and develops people in blended roles for exactly this reason.

Choose your hybrid lens

Every Resident learns the core product craft. Beyond that, you will lean into one of two hybrid paths, shaped by your interests and the product your team is building.

Product Strategy / Design Hybrid

A product strategist with design fluency, who shapes a proposition and proves it through design artifacts rather than long documents.

- Turn research and stakeholder input into a clear product concept, then express it as journey maps, flows and clickable prototypes.

- Use AI to go from interviews to a testable prototype quickly, and bring the craft and judgment to know when the result is good enough to put in front of users.

- Work side by side with Design Residents on usability testing, and let what users do, not what a deck says, drive the next decision.

A good fit if you are curious about users, like making ideas tangible, and enjoy workshops and storytelling.

Product Strategy / Technology Hybrid

A product strategist with technology depth, who turns business intent into technically grounded direction and keeps feasibility honest.

- Translate goals into well-formed requirements and user stories that engineers and AI coding tools can act on.

- Build the technical fluency to discuss APIs, data, CI/CD and architecture trade-offs, and to plan scope, dependencies and capacity, including work done by AI agents.

- Work with Engineering Residents to decide what to build, buy or skip, and to check what AI-assisted development produces.

A good fit if you are drawn to how things work under the hood, like structured problem solving, and want to speak credibly with engineers.

Not sure which one fits? That is normal. Tell us what you are drawn to in your application, and we will help you find your path during the program.

What you will do

You will contribute to a real product backlog, run light user research, and help make sure your team builds the right thing for the right users. Typical work includes:

- Research and strategy. Combine market analysis, stakeholder interviews and AI-assisted synthesis to uncover product opportunities and test your hypotheses with real users.

- Requirements and specs. Turn high-level goals and "fuzzy" concepts into precise requirements, user stories and context that both people and AI tools can build from.

- Rapid prototyping. Use AI-assisted tools to turn ideas into prototypes or working demos, and put them in front of users early.

- Agile delivery. Practice Agile principles with your team: backlog ownership, sprint rituals, and iterative, value-driven delivery.

- Roadmapping and prioritization. Build outcome-focused roadmaps that balance vision, technical feasibility and constraints, and prioritize with evidence.

- Verification and quality. Review AI-generated research, specs and code with a critical eye, and help define how the team will know the product works.

- Storytelling and presentation. Turn complex data into clear narratives that win alignment, and present your team's progress and recommendations.

- AI scouting. Explore where generative AI can speed up the team's workflow or unlock new value, and be honest about where it does not help.

What you will learn

The residency is built around three learning areas, with AI fluency woven through each.

- Product management. Identifying needs, defining strategy, and coordinating teams to deliver valuable solutions across transformation, strategy and build.

- Consulting. Analytical problem solving, clear communication and relationship skills used to deliver expert advice, including how to translate what AI can and cannot do into client value.

- Leadership. Setting a clear vision, driving cross-functional alignment, and helping teams adopt new ways of working, including working effectively with AI agents.

Who we are looking for

No previous product management experience is required. We care more about curiosity and judgment than a particular resume.

- A strong interest in technology, digital products and how businesses operate.

- An interest in product management and a basic understanding of PM methodology, with a passion for creating great experiences.

- Hands-on curiosity about AI tools: you have experimented with them for school, work or personal projects, and you can say what worked and what did not.

- Excellent written and verbal communication, and comfort presenting ideas clearly.

- A proactive, self-motivated approach, and eagerness to learn.

- Comfort working in a team and balancing multiple learning opportunities.

Bonus

- Familiarity with the software development lifecycle (SDLC), Agile principles, AI development lifecycle (AIDLC)

- Experience creating simple stories, flows, wireframes or prototypes.

- Experience with, or interest in, design, data, or technical fields such as software engineering, which will help you in a hybrid path.

Preferred Background

You are currently pursuing or have recently completed a degree in business, economics, computer science, information systems, data science, human-computer interaction, design, cognitive science or psychology, or a related field. We also hire Residents from non-traditional backgrounds as part of our effort to support career transitioners. If you are passionate about product management and have invested in your learning in other ways, we would love to hear about it.

Why Residency?

As a resident you’ll dive deep into end-to-end product development, receive direct mentorship in your area of interest from industry experts, and work alongside your peers to build a digital product - all while experiencing life inside of a global digital consultancy. Whether your passion lies in product management, program management design, data, or software engineering, this program offers an immersive, hands-on experience.

We believe in work/life balance. Seriously. We offer a ton of competitive perks, including:

- Expert Craft Mentorship: Receive personalized, one-on-one guidance from dedicated senior experts within your specific discipline (e.g., Product, Engineering, Design).

- High-Autonomy & Trust: Be treated as an integrated team member with the autonomy to own your work in an environment that prioritizes trust and work-life balance.

- Dynamic Work Community: Benefit from a flexible hybrid model balanced with intentional, in-person community-building events, social outings, and networking opportunities.

- Accelerated Career Development: Access customized workshops and focused resources designed to transition residents directly into full-time consulting roles.

- Cross-Disciplinary Collaboration: Work shoulder-to-shoulder with residents from all functional areas to master collaboration within a complete product development team.

- Competitive Compensation: Receive competitive program compensation of $20/hr. and benefits, including grubhub food delivery, office lunches, & social outings.

Next Steps

If Method sounds like the place for you, please submit an application by going to method.com/residency and looking for job postings titled “residency”.

To learn more, please visit our Residency Resource & FAQ Hub.

About the Program

Keysight's AI team builds adaptive engineering intelligence systems where measurement, simulation, and machine learning converge - models that learn from complex physical data and adapt to new design and testing conditions.

Role Overview

You will design, build, and evaluate an autonomous agentic workflow for a defined engineering process. The system will interpret incoming information, determine appropriate next steps, use approved tools to complete tasks, track progress, and incorporate feedback as the workflow evolves.

A central constraint is that the system's actions must be bounded, auditable, and recoverable. Engineers need to understand what it did, why it acted, what remains open, and where approval is required. You will develop evaluations for task completion, continuity, reliability, and human intervention. You will work alongside AI researchers, software engineers, and engineering stakeholders for the selected workflows.

Learning outcomes include applying agentic AI to realistic multi-step engineering workflows; designing stateful AI systems with durable context, provenance, recovery, and human approval points; evaluating continuity, reliability, completion rate, and intervention rate for non-deterministic systems; and building fluency with tool integration, workflow automation, task state management, and auditability requirements.

- Build an autonomous agentic workflow that maintains task state and context across multiple steps and sessions.
- Develop tool integrations connecting the system to approved communication, planning, document, workflow, and engineering applications.
- Implement mechanisms for incorporating new information, updating task state, and resuming incomplete work.
- Develop appropriate state and provenance mechanisms for decisions, actions, outcomes, and feedback.
- Design guardrails for approval, permissions, bounded actions, failure recovery, and escalation.
- Assemble representative engineering workflows and measure completion rate, reliability, continuity, and human intervention against a suitable baseline.

- Currently pursuing or recently completed a PhD in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Electrical or Electronic Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical field, with experience building and evaluating agent systems.
- Strong Python and software engineering: modular code, version control, reproducible pipelines.

- Demonstrated rigor in evaluating non-deterministic systems: benchmark design, held-out test sets, automated scoring, and a healthy distrust of demonstrations.
